ai-at-work.title: Trump drops restrictions on Anthropic’s Mythos and Fable models
ai-at-work.excerpt: The Trump administration's erratic approach to AI policymaking has left companies across the industry with little clarity about what will govern future model releases.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: The Trump administration lifted restrictions on Anthropic's Mythos and Fable models, reversing previous limitations on the AI company's development. This matters because digital workplace teams relying on AI tools need stable regulatory ground to plan deployments and budget appropriately, not policy whiplash. Here's the thing though: companies betting their knowledge management strategy on AI infrastructure that could flip with every administration change are basically building on quicksand.

ai-at-work.title: Wayve launches $85M employee tender offer at $8.5B valuation
ai-at-work.excerpt: Wayve’s offering is part of a growing trend of AI startups using employee tenders as a strategic tool to attract and retain talent.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Wayve, an autonomous driving AI company, is letting employees cash out some of their equity stakes at an $8.5 billion company valuation through an $85 million tender offer. This matters because it signals how competitive talent retention has become in AI companies, where stock options alone no longer cut it when engineers can walk next door for better deals. Here's the thing though: if your company needs to hand out $85 million just to keep people from leaving, that's either a sign of serious burnout or that you've got a real talent problem hiding underneath the valuation.

ai-at-work.title: The DeepMind trio who built a poker AI are now making money for quant hedge funds
ai-at-work.excerpt: EquiLibre Technologies, a Prague-based AI lab founded by three ex-DeepMind researchers, is now valued at more than $500 million.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Three former DeepMind researchers spun out a company called EquiLibre Technologies that's now worth over half a billion dollars by applying AI to quantitative hedge fund trading. This matters to digital workplace folks because it shows how talent mobility and specialized AI skills are reshaping where smart people work and how companies compete for them. Turns out the real money isn't in game theory, it's in making rich people richer faster, which honestly tracks perfectly with how capitalism actually works.

ai-at-work.title: Acti puts AI agents directly into your smartphone keyboard
ai-at-work.excerpt: Acti is betting the smartphone keyboard is the next home for AI assistants. The startup's new keyboard for iOS and Android works across apps and lets users create custom AI-powered shortcuts using nat
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Acti launched a smartphone keyboard that embeds AI agents directly into your typing interface, allowing custom shortcuts through natural language across any app. This matters because it's testing whether the keyboard could become the primary interface for AI assistance instead of chat windows or dedicated apps, which would fundamentally change how workers access AI tools throughout their day. My take: if this actually works smoothly, it could be genuinely useful for knowledge workers. But if it's another "AI everywhere" solution searching for a problem, we'll be deleting it faster than we delete unread Slack notifications.

tools-tech.title: Apple rushed to squash 29 bugs because AI is supercharging hackers - update ASAP
tools-tech.excerpt: Software updates are rolling out now for iPhone, iPad, and Mac, bringing fixes that weren't supposed to arrive so soon. Here's why.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Apple dropped emergency security patches for iPhones, iPads, and Macs after discovering that AI tools are making it easier for hackers to find and exploit vulnerabilities faster than ever before. For digital workplace teams managing Apple devices at scale, this means your MDM policies need to shift from "update eventually" to "update immediately or accept the risk." After three decades of watching security theater, I'll say this plainly: if your organization isn't patching within 48 hours of these releases, you're not being agile, you're being negligent.

tools-tech.title: 61% of US adults use AI for health information now - up from 2% in 2024
tools-tech.excerpt: Patients are also three times more likely to trust AI in their doctor's secure portal than a public chatbot.
tools-tech.dwp_take: More than six in ten Americans are now turning to AI for health information, a dramatic jump from basically nobody just last year. This matters to digital workplace folks because your employees are increasingly relying on AI for personal health decisions, which means your health benefits comms and wellness platforms need to acknowledge this shift or risk looking stuck in 2023. The really interesting bit is that people trust AI way more when it's baked into secure, official systems rather than free chatbots, which tells you everything about how critical trustworthy integrations are going to be.

tools-tech.title: Why 'countdown mode' is the task manager feature I can't live without
tools-tech.excerpt: This setting meshes perfectly with how my brain works, and I don't miss deadlines anymore.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Someone figured out that a visual countdown timer in their task manager stops them from procrastinating and missing deadlines. This matters because task management adoption fails when features don't match how people actually think, and "countdown mode" clearly hits that cognitive trigger for urgency that spreadsheets never will. The real insight here isn't the feature itself, it's that after thirty years of watching people struggle with productivity tools, the ones that stick are the ones that create artificial scarcity in your brain, and apparently staring at a ticking clock does that better than any motivational poster ever could.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft unveils Memora to tackle AI agents’ memory problem
tools-tech.excerpt: With AI agents increasingly expected to remember conversations, preferences, and decisions over extended periods, Microsoft Research has developed Memora, a memory system designed to provide more scal
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft built Memora, a new memory system that lets AI agents remember conversations and preferences over weeks or months instead of just forgetting everything after each chat session. This matters because digital workplace tools increasingly rely on AI agents handling complex workflows, and if they can't remember what they learned about your preferences or past decisions, you're basically training the same chatbot every single Monday. Finally, after years of AI that forgets you exist the moment you close the tab, someone's actually solving the problem that makes AI assistants feel like they have the memory span of a goldfish with WiFi issues.

digital-culture.title: How to stay productive when the future feels uncertain
digital-culture.excerpt: Right now, we’re living in a period of significant uncertainty about the future. AI is having a significant (but unknown) influence on the future of work. Global instability is making it more difficul
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company's piece argues that uncertainty about AI, geopolitics, and economic instability is making it harder for workers to stay focused and productive. This matters because digital workplace leaders need to understand that productivity challenges right now aren't about Slack settings or standing desks, they're about genuine anxiety over what work looks like in two years. My take: the article basically says "uncertainty makes concentration hard," which is true but hardly revolutionary, and I'd rather see advice on how to actually build psychological safety in your org so people can work despite the chaos.

digital-culture.title: How to boost brain health at work in the age of AI
digital-culture.excerpt: AI has quickly become embedded in our everyday work, from drafting emails to synthesizing research and making decisions. In my roles as a medical doctor and business consultant, I talk to many corpora
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company ran a piece arguing that AI's integration into daily work tasks is raising questions about cognitive health, not just productivity gains. This matters because digital workplace leaders are finally waking up to the fact that outsourcing your brain to AI all day might actually atrophy the thing you need to do actual work. Here's my take after three decades: we've spent years optimizing for speed and efficiency, and now we're realizing we may have outsourced the thinking that made us valuable in the first place.

digital-culture.title: The Trump Administration Is Lifting Its Export Controls on Anthropic’s Mythos and Fable AI Models
digital-culture.excerpt: The White House is easing restrictions on Anthropic’s most advanced AI models weeks after ordering the company to suspend access for foreign nationals.
digital-culture.dwp_take: The Trump administration reversed course and lifted export restrictions on Anthropic's advanced AI models just weeks after imposing them on foreign nationals. This matters to digital workplace folks because AI tools are becoming core productivity infrastructure, and unpredictable regulatory whiplash makes it harder to plan enterprise deployments with any confidence. Look, if your C-suite is trying to decide whether to bet on an AI platform, watching Washington ping-pong the rules probably isn't helping anyone sleep at night.

digital-culture.title: Truckloads of Tesla Batteries Keep Getting Stolen Before They Even Leave the Factory
digital-culture.excerpt: Nine major suspected cargo thefts happened at Tesla’s Nevada battery factory in January alone, according to sheriff’s records obtained by WIRED.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Tesla's Nevada battery factory had nine suspected cargo thefts in January alone, with finished batteries disappearing before they even left the facility. For digital workplace folks, this is a stark reminder that physical security and supply chain visibility need the same rigor you'd apply to cybersecurity, because a stolen battery is a breach of a different kind. Turns out the weakest link in your operation might not be the guy who forgets his password, but the actual guy who just drives off with a truck full of your inventory.
